correctness.rationale: The RKHS squared error is minimized exactly over the one-node weight, yielding g^T R_j g with PSD R_j. For arbitrary p, the spectral masses v_i are nonnegative and sum to one; eigenvector Rayleigh quotients imply the unique water-filling lower bound t. Pairwise simplex mass gives t>=lambda_i lambda_j/(lambda_i+lambda_j), and the source RP expected-residual formula then gives W_RP<=(r-1)t. At rank two both nonzero RP eigenvalues coincide with t, closing the lower bound for every eigenbasis. For a positive diagonal kernel the water-filled probabilities attain t, and explicit diagonal-M witnesses approach r-1. Rational exact checker independently reconstructs the mean residual and witness identities; no finite experiment is used to prove the universal theorem.

value.rationale: The one-pivot node law is a natural primitive of numerical kernel compression and Mercer-free RKHS quadrature. The result supplies an exact positive rank-two universality guarantee, a sharp negative rank-dependent failure mode, and an actionable diagonal-kernel optimal alternative; the distinction matters because the source RP rule is tuned to trace-based quality, while a target-oblivious integrator may want a uniform mean-squared accuracy guarantee. The gap grows unboundedly with rank, is not a tiny or arbitrary finite slice, and directly explains the tradeoff between the commonly used sampling rule and an independently natural minimax performance criterion.
